What is Base? How does it work?
What Base offers depends on your address. In many power-to-choose areas across Texas, you can choose Base Backup + Energy, which pairs a home battery with electricity service, or Base Energy if you just want an energy plan. Both come with a fixed, low energy rate to keep your costs predictable. In other areas, we work with utility partners who offer a battery program through your existing utility, so your energy provider doesn't change. When your plan includes a 39.2 kWh battery, it helps balance the grid, charging when demand is low and sending power back when the grid needs support. During an outage it automatically powers your home, usually without you noticing the switch. Our current battery system protects against 97% of outages. Enter your zip code to see what's available for your home.
How much does Base cost? How much will I pay for energy?

Your exact costs depend on your address and plan, so enter your zip code for a precise quote. Here's how pricing is structured:

Getting started

A small refundable deposit that applies toward your one-time installation cost once your battery is installed
A one-time installation fee that varies by zip code and plan, with your deposit credited toward it
In some utility-partnership areas, installation is discounted or waived

Ongoing costs

A flat monthly membership fee, based on your plan
Some utility partnerships waive the monthly membership fee

Monthly energy bills

When Base is your energy provider, you pay a fixed, low energy rate plus your utility's transmission and delivery fees
If you have solar panels, Base buys back any excess energy you produce
Where Base only provides your battery, you keep your existing energy provider and bill, and Base doesn't charge an energy rate

You can see Base's latest plans and Electricity Facts Labels (EFLs) here. Use our bill comparison tool to see how much you could save with Base.

Why is Base significantly less expensive than alternatives?
Base's shared business model is what sets it apart. Base earns income from the power grid instead of from members. That's how you can get whole-home backup without paying for an expensive traditional generator, or the massive upfront investment of a solar system and battery that can take longer to pay back than it lasts. With Base, you pay just a one-time installation cost for the team of electricians who install your battery. Because revenue comes from the grid, not from members, Base avoids hidden fees and surprise rate hikes.
How can I refer a friend who's interested in Base? Do you have a referral program?

Base has a referral program, and members are a big part of how word spreads and more neighborhoods get involved.

Existing members can send friends, family, neighbors, or strangers their personal referral link, which you can access in your Base account.

Refer a friend and you both earn a reward when they get set up with Base. For most members that's a free month of power, or a bill credit if you have solar. Rewards can vary by area and plan.

How does Base make money?
Base operates differently from traditional power companies. Instead of profiting directly from members, Base earns revenue by using grid-balancing software paired with outage prediction technology. This approach optimizes the Base battery for both grid stability and outage protection. When the grid is functioning, Base uses its batteries to support grid balancing. This strengthens the grid's resilience and generates income for Base. By leveraging its network of batteries for grid balancing, Base maintains low rates for members while remaining profitable.
